posts.content_md:
This is my latest hologram, I made last week:

It show's an electronic evaluation board for a microcontroller. 

It's a rainbow copy on PFG-01, it is 8x10" (19x25 cm)

big collimating mirror?

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md: Nice indeed. What color was the circuit board (and laser)? It looks like a diffuser was used for object lighting -if so, this worked out well to eliminate confusing shadows and excessively bright specular reflections.

posts.author: HoloM
posts.content_md: It's an image plane hologram the board comes out about 6 cm. I made it with a 40cm collimating mirror, yes HeNe. The Laser was red the circuit board green. I only used a lens for object lightning

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Very very nice. How large was the master? How wide was the slit? Is the reason we are seeing all green because the hologram is illuminated with a green laser instead of white light. I would expect more of a rainbow smear replay with an object that size in the Rainbow format. Again great looking hologram.

posts.author: HoloM
posts.content_md:
The Master was about 40cm wide, the slit 5-6 mm. No, it's illuminated with white light. the distance of photographing was about 50 cm I think. In this distance you see the whole hologram in nearly one color. 

here are a few other pictures, with the same illumination, but other position of the camera.

Here you see a picture of the original circuit board, only the LEDs on this photo are different.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
> **HoloM:** It's an image plane hologram the board comes out about 6 cm. I made it with a 40cm collimating mirror, yes HeNe. The Laser was red the circuit board green. I only used a lens for object lightning

The board came out brighter than I would have expected, but then it was a non-saturated whitish green. And now that I know there was no diffuser for lighting, I can see the shadows easily Very good photos, by the way.
